unit_vs_integration_boundary.principle: Unit tests isolate the new pure/DB-touching helper functions in masterDataSchema.js with a stubbed or real-but-scoped pool. Integration tests exercise the shared masterDataRouter.js factory end-to-end against the live/test Postgres schema for the resource_cost table specifically, since the FK-existence check and the LEFT JOIN are inherently DB-dependent behavior that a pure mock would only restate, not verify.
unit_scope: backend/src/masterDataSchema.js:validateReferences — mock pool.query to return zero/one rows and assert: (a) throws validationError with the correct field key + message when the referenced employeeId does not exist, (b) does not throw when it does, (c) is skipped entirely when the field is optional and omitted, (d) is skipped for an explicit null on a non-required reference field (the 'clearing it' case, mirroring validateBody's existing null-handling tests), (e) required-but-missing-on-create is already caught by validateBody before this ever runs (assert the sequencing contract, not duplicate the check)

backend/src/masterDataSchema.js:lookupJoinSql / lookupSelectSql (pure string builders, table.lookups is fixed descriptor data — no DB needed) — assert the generated SQL for resource_cost's lookups descriptor: correct alias (lookup_0), correct ON clause (foreignColumn = table.localColumn), the added 'and lookup_0.deleted_at is null' soft-delete predicate, and correct projection column aliases (lookup_0_name, lookup_0_designation)

backend/src/masterDataSchema.js:toResponse for resource_cost — feed a row object with lookup_0_name/lookup_0_designation present (simulates a GET's joined row) and again with them absent (simulates a POST/PATCH's bare 'returning *' row) and assert employeeName/employeeDesignation are the joined values in the first case and exactly null (not undefined) in the second, plus offshoreCost/onsiteCost pass through as null when the DB column is null

mcp-server/src/masterDataTables.js's resource_cost field list (pure data, no network) — assert employeeId/offshoreCost/onsiteCost are present with type: 'number', employeeId is required, and employeeName/employeeDesignation are absent from the writable field list (locks in 'read-only lookup, never a writable MCP field')
integration_scope: backend/src/masterDataRouter.js against resource_cost, run against a real (test/dev) Postgres connection per the existing masterDataSchema.test.js style of exercising real DB behavior where the logic is DB-shaped: POST with a non-existent employeeId returns 422 with a validation_error body (not a raw Postgres 500) before any row is inserted; POST with a valid employeeId that exists in resources succeeds and the row is retrievable; GET /resource_cost and GET /resource_cost/:id both return employeeName/employeeDesignation correctly resolved from the current resources row for that employeeId; updating the underlying resources.name/designation and re-fetching resource_cost shows the updated values (locks in 'live lookup, not a stored/stale copy' — this is the single most important behavioral assertion for this feature, since a stale-copy regression would be invisible from resource_cost's own table alone); a soft-deleted resources row (deleted_at set) yields employeeName/employeeDesignation === null on the resource_cost side, not the old values; GET / (list) for resource_cost does not 500 (locks in the sortColumn fix — this is exactly the round-1 regression architecture-critic/solution-architect already fixed, and it must have a regression test now that the fix exists, not just a manual verification note); PATCH can independently set/null offshoreCost and onsiteCost without touching the other (locks in 'independently optional, no cross-field rule')

mcp-server's add_resource_cost/update_resource_cost tools (mcp-server/src/index.js's zod-generated handlers) — with apiClient.js's HTTP call mocked at the fetch/apiClient boundary (not the backend), assert: employeeId is required and typed as a number by the zod schema (a string or missing employeeId is rejected before any HTTP call is made); a backend 422 (FK-not-found) response is surfaced as {isError: true, ...} with the real message, not swallowed or generalized; employeeName/employeeDesignation are not accepted as input parameters on either tool
explicitly_out_of_scope_for_this_feature: The other 8 master-data tables' router/schema code paths — sortColumn/lookups/references are opt-in descriptor keys that default to prior behavior; no regression tests needed for tables that don't set them (CLAUDE.md §1 Minimal Impact — this stage doesn't retrofit coverage onto untouched tables)
FEAT-7's positionId (deliberately unvalidated, modules.practiceId-style) — separate feature, separate queue entry, out of scope here

Any resource_cost frontend form/pick-list component — none exists or is planned; the dashboard is read-only for this table per the task, so MasterDataTable's existing generic-component tests (already covering loading/error/empty/success states from FEAT-1) are sufficient without a resource_cost-specific frontend test

mock_strategy.database: Unit-level tests for validateReferences mock pool.query directly (vi/node:test's built-in mocking or a hand-rolled stub object, matching whatever minimal-dependency style backend/src/masterDataSchema.test.js already uses) so the FK-existence branch logic is tested without a live connection. Integration-level tests for the router (GET/POST/PATCH against resource_cost, including the live-lookup and sortColumn assertions) run against a real Postgres connection — mocking the LEFT JOIN and its soft-delete predicate would just restate the SQL string being tested rather than verify it actually resolves correctly, which is the one property this feature most needs proven.
mock_strategy.mcp_server: apiClient.js's HTTP layer is mocked (not the backend) when testing the MCP tool handlers, so tool-level tests assert request shaping (numeric employeeId, no employeeName/employeeDesignation params) and error-surfacing without needing a running backend process — consistent with 'validate at system boundaries, MCP just forwards' from the architecture stages.
mock_strategy.no_snapshot_tests: Per frontend.md (extended here to backend/mcp-server response-shape assertions by convention): all assertions are explicit field/value checks, never snapshot dumps of a full response object.
